To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the NLO QCD corrections for the production of a Higgs-bosons in hadron-harmon collisions are very large, that they are positive and that they are almost completely independent of the choice of the renormalization and factorization scale.

we have computed the next-to-leading order QED corrections to the process e+e−→μ+μ−γ, which is a very important background for searches of Higgs bosons at e+e− colliders, and that we have found that the corrections are very large, and that the corrections are not negligible even for small values of the photon energy.

the next-to-leading order QED corrections to the production of a Higgs boson in association with an electron and a neutrino in e + e - collisions are small and do not exceed a few percent of the leading order result.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the next-to-leading order QED corrections to the production of a heavy quarkonium state Q Q ′ in e + e − annihilation.
the calculation of the differential distributions for Higgs boson in next-to-leading order Qcd.
the study of Higgs bosons produced in hadron-haradron collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the NLO QCD corrections to the differential distributions d 3 σ/dpT H/dyH/dpT X ′ for the semi-inclusively produced Higgs boson in hadronic collisions are large and of the order of 30% in the kinematic region 100 GeV < m H < 200 Gev and 10 < pT H < 50 Gev.
the next-to-leading order corrections to the total inclusive cross section are small, of the order 10%.

the next-to-leading order corrections to the inclusive Higgs production cross section are large, of the order of + 40% at √s = 14 TeV and + 50% at √s= 100 TeV, and that the corrections to the differential distributions are even larger.
we present for the first time the full next-toleading order corrected differential distributions for the process p+p → H + ′X ′ in hadron-hadrone collisions.
the NLO corrections are large for the total cross section and the differential distributions, and the NLO K-factors are strongly pT and y dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the next-to-leading order corrections to the total cross section are about 10% and the next-to-leading corrections to the distributions d 2σ/dpT /d y, dσ/d pT and dσ/ dy are typically of the order 10% to 30%, with the exception of the region pT < 20 GeV where they are about 50%.
next-to-leading order Q CD corrections to the differential cross sections d 2 σ/ dpT /dy, ds/dpT and ds/dy are large and negative, especially at small transverse momenta pT.
next-to-leading order Qcd corrections are very large for all distributions, and they are of the order of 30 % for dσ/dp /dy and 50 % for dσ /dy at the Tevatron.
